rationale: The provided literature confirms a broad genotype-phenotype correlation in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #620988) where loss-of-function (LoF) variants associate with milder neurodevelopmental phenotypes and nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense variants associate with severe NDD and cytoplasmic accumulation. However, the specific hypothesis that exactly 100% of individuals with NLS variants exhibit severe expressive speech impairment/non-verbal status while all LoF patients achieve phrase or sentence speech is not supported by the data in the provided literature block. The sources lack granular speech milestone numerators/denominators demonstrating a strict, non-overlapping 100% speech dichotomy across these variant classes.

evidence.text: Calame et al. (2023) identified 20 individuals with de novo DHX9 variants and performed quantitative HPO analysis demonstrating that LoF variants associate with mild NDD phenotypes and NLS missense variants cause severe NDD phenotypes, accompanied by cytoplasmic accumulation of DHX9.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact numerators and denominators for absent speech (HP:0001344) versus phrase/sentence speech in DHX9 cohorts stratified strictly by variant class (LoF, NLS missense, non-NLS missense)?
new_directions.rationale: Case-level deep phenotyping data from larger collaborative registries (such as ERN-ITHACA) are needed to substantiate whether speech milestones strictly track with NLS mislocalization or exhibit variable expressivity.
